cues: A family of standard forms is built around a squared plus or minus x squared.
One over x squared plus a squared gives inverse tan.
One over root of a squared minus x squared gives inverse sine.
To use them, first make the coefficient of x squared equal to one, and complete the square if there is an x term.
text: A family of standard forms is built around a squared plus or minus x squared. One over x squared plus a squared gives inverse tan. One over root of a squared minus x squared gives inverse sine. And others give logarithms. To use them, first make the coefficient of x squared equal to one, and complete the square if there is an x term.
